history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: this row is the same temple as seq 2244, whose file is being written as the PRIMARY record by another worker (id jambukeswarar-temple-thiruvanaikaval or similar). CSV TOWN FLAG: the CSV's 'Srirangam' is approximate - the temple is at THIRUVANAIKAVAL on Srirangam island, about 2.5 km from Srirangam town and ~11 km from Tiruchirappalli Junction. Sri Jambukeswarar Temple is one of the five Pancha Bhoota Sthalams of Shiva, representing the water element (Appu): the sanctum holds an Appu Lingam continuously surrounded by water from an underground spring that never fully disappears. Legend: Goddess Parvati as Akilandeswari performed penance here, worshipping a lingam made of Cauvery water under a Venn Navaal (Jambu) tree; Shiva granted her darshan and taught her spiritual wisdom. The spider and the elephant who worshipped here gave the place its name (Thiru-aanai-kaval, 'the holy elephant's grove'). It is one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams and one of the few major Tamil Shiva shrines where the goddess is treated as the principal independent deity. Notable traditions: the daily noon ucchikalam pooja performed by a priest dressed in female attire, and (per traditional accounts) the Sri Chakra Yantras installed by Adi Shankaracharya as Akilandeswari's ear ornaments. Antiquity claims rest on traditional Chola-era attributions; inscriptions from the Chola period are found in the temple.
